rows: I respect your position. I would just like to know why you think it is permanent.
Brawling is a fine tool. I am sure you use it more gracefully than most people.
The gamble is a bold move. I admire it, though I suspect it is not your own idea.
Time, to me, is charming. I wish I had your patience, honestly.
The people deserve the best contest, and I am happy to let you show them yours.
I am glad you asked, and I am going to answer it my way.
I have had every opportunity, and I am grateful for it. Some of us had to earn ours.
Might I check the stance? Beautiful. Very composed.
Technique, what a lovely word. You have clearly been well coached. Show me what you did yourself.
Strikes are impressive. I imagine someone helped you choose them.
The gamble is a lovely gesture. I wonder whose gesture it really is.
A stall is an elegant choice. I admire that you have the freedom to make it.
The people deserve a contest that is earned, not arranged. I think they will see the difference.
You say you are among the best, which is kind. I am sure that is a comfort to the people who helped you.
How lovely, your {strength}. Lovely. I wonder who taught you to be proud of it.
I have been admiring your {strength}, and I am curious about where it really comes from.
You are very composed, which I admire. Very good. It is hard to keep calm when you are not sure of your ground.
Very fair, then. You have made a fair point, and I will be fair back.
I could be rude about that. I would rather be pleasant and let the result speak.
One fall, kept lovely and simple. Keep me down, and I will admit you were the better man.
On the mat I will be polite. It is the most dangerous thing I can offer.
Grounded or standing, I am still smiling, and I still mean it.
Would you stand up to me? I would like to see what you do without help.
That was a polite answer. It sounded like it was your own.
Answer, please. I am sure you have a good reason. Give it.
Very fair, then. I respect that.
I concede that, politely. I will be polite about it at the bell.
I will wrestle this match politely, and I will see who really holds the advantage.
My approach is courteous. You will see what that means on the night.
Whatever happens, I hope you will remember I was gracious about it.
Still going. I am still being polite.
I have one kind remark left, and you will hear it when the bell rings.
How very fair of you to ask. I haven't a particular instance I can cite, and it would be rather ungracious to invent one.
I owe you the courtesy of an honest answer. I can't substantiate the allegation, so please disregard it.
Quite right. We can dispense with that little unpleasantness and have a proper match.
Thank you for making the distinction. Let us proceed without the unsupported charge.
We may establish who wrestles the better match, which is quite sufficient for this evening.
Let the referee judge the result and the audience judge how we earn it. That seems reasonable to me.
How interesting that the allegation has taken over the discussion. What can we actually demonstrate without relying on it?
Let us give the audience a fair opportunity to judge us. What can the contest show them that our words cannot?
How flattering that you've spent so much time studying my {strength}. I wonder how much of that defence you can execute without assistance.
You've made an elegant proposal for dealing with my {strength}. I shall be delighted to see you deliver it yourself.
Quite fair. I ought not to suggest certainty where there is none.
Thank you for the correction. I shall reserve judgement until we have something definite to discuss.
I admire your experience. I would be even more impressed if you could demonstrate its relevance to this particular encounter.
You have my respect for the years you've devoted to the craft. You have yet to secure my shoulders.
One hopes experience teaches the distinction between an opportunity and a trap.
I have learned that an elegant response is sometimes simply to abandon the move one intended.
How flattering that you've devoted your evenings to my work. I do hope you have allowed for a little improvisation.
I admire your diligence. It would be rather dull of me to give you precisely the same encounter.
I study the transitions that appear effortless. There is generally a rather considerable amount of work concealed in them.
I rehearse the less elegant alternatives too. One must be able to recover when the preferred movement proves impossible.
